questions.title: 喜欢或不喜欢的高建筑
questions.text:
Describe a tall building you like or dislike
You should say:
What it is used for
Where it is
What it looks like
And explain why you like/dislike it
questions.english:
A tall building I like is a residential tower in the city where I live in Guangdong. It is mainly used for apartments, with shared entrances and practical facilities for the residents.

The building has many floors and a fairly simple shape. I wouldn't call it a dramatic landmark. What I like is the balance between a modern appearance and everyday usefulness. The windows let in plenty of light, and the areas around the entrance feel clear and easy to understand.

I became interested in it because I live in an apartment myself, so I notice how residential buildings can make daily life easier or more difficult. A tower may look impressive from a distance, but the lifts, maintenance, and access to nearby services matter much more when people actually use it.

This building appeals to me because it seems designed for living rather than only for photographs. It offers a practical way to house people in a city without using too much land. I wouldn't choose a home simply because it is high up, but I appreciate a building that uses its height sensibly and still feels comfortable at ground level.
questions.chinese:
我喜欢的一座高楼，是我现在居住的广东城市里的一座住宅楼。它主要用于公寓居住，并为住户提供共同的出入口和实用设施。

这栋楼有很多层，整体造型比较简单。我不会把它称作一座特别引人注目的地标。我喜欢的是现代外观与日常实用性之间的平衡。窗户带来了充足的自然光，入口附近也显得清晰，让人容易辨认。

我之所以对它感兴趣，是因为我自己也住公寓，所以会留意住宅建筑怎样让日常生活更方便，或者更麻烦。一座高楼从远处看可能很气派，但当人们真正使用它时，电梯、维护情况以及能否方便地使用附近的服务，都重要得多。

这栋楼吸引我，是因为它看起来是为生活设计的，而不只是为了拍照。它提供了一种在城市里安排住房、又不占用过多土地的实用方式。我不会仅仅因为楼层高就选择一处住房，但我欣赏能够合理利用高度、同时在地面层面也让人感到舒适的建筑。
pending: 住宅塔楼、附近设施、外观采光与喜爱是完整候选；只确认用户住广东城市公寓，未确认所住楼高度或此楼真实存在。

questions.title: 有趣视频
questions.text:
Describe an interesting video
You should say:
When and where you watched it
What it is about
Why you watched it
And explain how you feel about it
questions.english:
An interesting video I watched showed a robot handling everyday objects. I watched it on my computer at home one evening when I wanted a short break from studying.

The robot had to identify items and place them in the right positions. The video didn't only show a perfect final result. It also included an attempt that went wrong and showed how the system tried again. That made it more interesting than a simple display of fast, impressive movements.

I watched it because my master's studies focus on AI and robotics. I wanted to see an example of a robot dealing with the physical world, where objects can move and small errors matter. Something that looks easy for a person can involve several difficult problems for a machine.

I felt curious and motivated afterwards. The most useful part was thinking about the gap between a successful demonstration and a reliable system people could use every day. I didn't regard the video as proof that the problem had been completely solved. Instead, it gave me a clear example to think about and reminded me why practical robotics remains such an interesting research area.
questions.chinese:
我看过的一个有趣视频，展示了一台机器人如何处理日常物品。某天晚上，我想在学习之余短暂休息一下，就在家里的电脑上看了这个视频。

机器人需要识别物品，再把它们放到正确的位置。视频并不只展示一个完美的最终结果，也包括了一次失败的尝试，以及系统如何重新尝试。相比单纯展示快速、令人惊艳的动作，这样的内容让我觉得更有趣。

我会看这个视频，是因为我的硕士学习重点是人工智能和机器人。我想看看机器人应对物理世界的例子：在这个世界里，物品会移动，细小的误差也很重要。一个对人来说看似简单的动作，对机器来说可能涉及好几个难题。

看完之后，我感到好奇，也更有动力。最有价值的是思考成功演示与人们能够日常使用的可靠系统之间还有什么差距。我没有把这个视频当作问题已经完全解决的证明，而是把它看作一个清晰、值得思考的例子。它也提醒我，为什么实用机器人仍然是如此有趣的研究领域。
pending: 具体视频、观看时间、失败重试画面和观看后感受为授权候选；未指定真实机器人系统或引用其能力。

questions.title: 帮助他人
questions.text: Can kids provide any help to parents?
questions.english: Children can help with age-appropriate tasks, such as putting away belongings, setting the table, or sorting simple items. Older children may assist with basic technology as well. The benefit isn't only reducing parents' workload; it also teaches cooperation and responsibility. Tasks should be safe and manageable, and children shouldn't be expected to carry responsibilities that properly belong to adults.
